reader.requirement: At --std 85, for MOVE, ADD and SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING, a data item of D1 and one of D2 are a candidate pair only when neither is FILLER (explicit or by an omitted data-name) and both have the same data-name and the same chain of qualifiers up to, but not including, D1 and D2 (names compared case-insensitively; a nameless FILLER group contributes no qualifier), with D1/D2 themselves possibly qualified or subscripted.

edition-consulted.switches: perPair = DialectLevel < 2002: at 85 each pair's place re-evaluates the group operands' subscripts (separate-MOVE equivalence, D-CORR85); from 2002 they are anchored at statement start. Subscript timing only; the name/qualifier match of this rule is not switched

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition/CobolVersion in CorrespondingBinder.cs: the one hit is line 119 (perPair). CorrMatch/CorrMembers/CorrEligible/NamesakeCounts consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for the pairing rule; only subscript-evaluation timing of the group operands differs, which is GR1 of the MOVE/ADD statements, not this rule)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb229 exercises FILLER groups and rule-4/5 exclusions at the top level; not mismatched qualifier chains at depth (same name under differently named or differently nested groups), group x elementary namesakes, D1/D2 qualified or subscripted, an omitted data-name (implicit FILLER), case-insensitive names, or an ODO table in D1

probes.printed: MATCH corr1.out: M1/M2 G2=11000000110000AB11 (K, Z, SE.T pair; M under SA vs SA.SB, N under SA.SB vs SA, Q under SC vs SQ, W top vs SW.W, FILLER: no pair; GE group x GE elementary pairs as a group move 'AB'); M3 (SA OF G1 TO SA OF G2) and M4 (SB TO SB) all zeros; A1 only K added (Z alphanumeric, GE group); S1 back to zeros
probes.expected: 'have the same data-name and the same qualifiers up to, but not including, D1 and D2' and not FILLER

probes.printed: MATCH corr2.out: C1 G2=11001100 (aa vs AA pairs, BB pairs, omitted-name items do not, OD OCCURS DEPENDING excluded); C2 MOVE CORR G3 TO EL (I) TB=000034120000; C3 ADD CORR G3 TO EL (3) TB=000034123412; C4 MOVE CORR EL (2) TO G3 G3=1234
probes.expected: an item described without a data-name is FILLER (no pair); a subscripted D1/D2 pairs by its subordinates' names; the OCCURS item is ignored (rule 4)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.3 GR1  (║6.4.3 The CORRESPONDING Phrase║)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: CorrMatch descends group x group namesakes level by level, so qualification identity is structural; CorrMembers walks through nameless groups (no qualifier) unless rule 4/5 cuts them off, the reading the 1985 text gives too since a FILLER group has no name to qualify by. Classes e and f do not bear on a name-matching rule; c: 1985 adds no form here that a later edition removed.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-021/corra.cob --std 85 (corra-002): MOVE CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2 gives G2=[R-U7Y]: P.R (D1) pairs P.FILLER-group.R (D2) (a nameless group adds no qualifier, chain P on both sides); P.Q.S does not pair P.T.S (qualifier Q vs T at depth); FILLER-group.U pairs top-level U; V pairs; Y pairs FILLER.FILLER.Y. ADD CORRESPONDING H1 TO H2 = [00]: P.C1 vs top C1 and top C2 vs P.C2 (same name, different qualifier chains) do not pair. These complement the reader's corr1/corr2 (mismatched chains at depth one, case-insensitive names, subscripted D1/D2, omitted-name FILLER, OCCURS exclusion). Reading taken: a data item subordinate to a FILLER group is not itself 'designated by the key word FILLER', and FILLER cannot be a qualifier, so it pairs; the text does not exclude it. A first draft putting a condition-name in D1 under the same word as a D2 data-name drew COBOL2692 (user-defined word in two classes), a separate rule. cite: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.3 GR1 'the same qualifiers up to, but not including, D1 and D2'.
